---
title: "Python"
---

The code blocks on this site are illustrative and are not executed: every
example would call SIDOF or the DOF website. The
[developer docs](https://legistlan.github.io/dofjson/dev/) hold the live,
verified examples.

## One entry point

`dofjson.sidof` talks to SIDOF, the preferred source, which exposes a REST
API; `dofjson.dofweb` talks to the DOF's own website, used to recover the days
and legal provisions SIDOF is missing outright. A caller never needs to import
either, or to decide which of the two has what it needs: every function they
offer is reachable straight off the `dofjson` package.

```python
import dofjson

dofjson.get_nota(4997808)               # SIDOF has it, or the website does
dofjson.get_notas(dt.date(1999, 3, 8))  # a day SIDOF lost, recovered from the website
dofjson.download_nota_pdf(4997808, outdir)
```

## Reading a legal provision or a day

`get_nota(codNota)` and `get_notas(date)` try SIDOF first and fall back to the
website automatically. The result says where it came from in `fuente`:
`dofjson.titulos.FUENTE_PREDETERMINADA` (`"sidof"`) or `dofjson.FUENTE_WEB`
(`"dof.gob.mx"`).

```python
dofjson.get_nota(4997808)["cadenaContenido"]      # the legal provision's HTML text
dofjson.get_notas(date)                           # respaldo="todos" by default
dofjson.get_notas(date, respaldo="nunca")         # trust SIDOF alone
```

A single call to the library defaults to `respaldo="todos"` (always
double-check an empty day), unlike the command line's `--archivo`, which
defaults to `"habiles"`: a one-off query has no 40,000-day request budget to
mind. A legal provision the website has no HTML for comes back with
`existeHtml` `"N"`, and an unknown `codNota` with `"Nota": []`, as SIDOF
answers.

## Downloads

```python
dofjson.download_nota(4997808, outdir)
dofjson.download_nota_imagenes(4997808, outdir)
dofjson.download_nota_pdf(4997808, outdir)
dofjson.download_nota_imagen_o_pdf(4997808, outdir)
dofjson.download_edicion_pdf(dt.date(2026, 6, 16), "VES", outdir)
```

- `download_nota` saves a legal provision's JSON.
- `download_nota_imagenes` downloads its scanned page image(s).
- `download_nota_pdf` produces the provision as its own PDF: the edition PDF
  (there is no per-provision PDF endpoint) sliced to the provision's pages with
  `pypdf`. The edition PDF is cached in `outdir` as `edicion-{codDiario}.pdf`,
  so slicing another provision from the same edition does not fetch it again.
- `download_nota_imagen_o_pdf` tries the page image first and falls back to the
  whole, uncut edition PDF, cached the same way. It is meant for bulk-downloading
  everything a large batch of provisions without HTML needs into one `outdir`.
- `download_edicion_pdf` downloads a whole edition's PDF given only its date and
  edition (`MAT`, `VES` or `EXT`).

These downloads only ever fetch from SIDOF: the website carries no
per-provision images, PDFs or page numbers. They still resolve a bare
`codNota` through `get_nota()`, so a provision SIDOF has no record of raises a
clear error.

## Plain passthroughs

`get_diario`, `get_indicadores`, `get_imagenes`, `download_pdf` and
`download_imagen` have nothing to resolve and call SIDOF directly.

## A day as one flat sequence

`get_notas(date)` answers the day split into its three editions
(`NotasMatutinas`, `NotasVespertinas`, `NotasExtraordinarias`, plus the
day-level `fuente`), which is the wire shape of both sources. To go through the
whole day without knowing those key names, and without losing which edition a
note came from:

```python
for nota in dofjson.fetch_daily_legal_provisions(dt.date(2026, 7, 15)):
    print(nota["edicion"], nota["codNota"], nota["titulo"])   # MAT, then VES, then EXT
```

It takes either the date or a response already in hand, in which case nothing
is fetched. Every note is a shallow copy of the original, ordered edition-first
and by `codNota` inside an edition, carrying two extra keys: `edicion` and the
day's `fuente`. An empty day gives `[]`. The pure half of this, for a response
already in hand, is `dofjson.notas_del_dia(notas)`.

## Helpers over a fetched day

- `infer_paginas(nota, notas_del_dia)` infers which page(s) a note occupies,
  from the fact that notes are published one after another: if the next note
  starts on the same page, this one is confined to it; if it starts later, this
  one is assumed to span through that page.
- `quita_notas_sin_titulo(notas_del_dia)` drops the notes with no `titulo` from
  a `get_notas()` response, to build a clean per-day index. Do not use it on the
  response passed into `infer_paginas`.
